utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Nice: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, the OSCE, as you know, reported regularly on what they observed. Do you have any reason to doubt the accuracy of their observations generally?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes and no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why yes?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because sometimes their information was not objective.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Give me an example.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The example of Kacanik, for instance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll come to Kacanik later. Anything in relation to the earlier period or Racak?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't read their reports on Racak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Before I come to look at some of their reporting, Shukri Buja was the KLA leader in your area, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He made a statement in the course of 2001, which is an exhibit in this case. It's Exhibit 212, which we're going to look at. Tell me, by September 2001, the Serbs had left and the -- not the KLA, but the interests served by the KLA were in the ascendancy in Kosovo; correct?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The interests of the KLA in the sense of the interests of the Serbs? I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The interests of --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Serbs had left Kosovo in large numbers.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were expelled. They did not leave of their own accord.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those seeking independence for Kosovo, or even the irredentists seeking joinder with Albania, were better placed in 2001 than they were in 1999; correct?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course they were in a better position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I want to know is, right before we start looking at his statement, are you going to be able to give any reason why Shukri Buja should tell untruths in the year 2001 about the deployment of his forces in Racak and thereabouts in January of 1999? Can you think of any reason why such a man should tell untruths about that part of his own history?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That's a very difficult question to answer. I mean, in the adversarial system it's one of the golden rules that you don't ask a witness to comment on what someone else may have been thinking or what they may have given evidence about before. You should ask them what they saw or knew or heard themselves. It's impossible for this man to answer it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I highly disagree with my learned friend. He has expressed general knowledge about the area, and we know that what happens is that when witnesses are confronted with things that they find difficult, they sometimes say - I'm not, of course, suggesting it about this witness - that the person has made something up and then they have to give a reason for it. I want to know if this witness can identify now, in advance, any reason that he can think of from the circumstances why a supporter of the KLA should, in 2001, be untruthful about what had gone before. He may not be able to answer, but if he can, I'd like his assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'll allow the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You will have to ask Shukri Buja that, first and foremost. I've never spoken to him. I don't know what he thinks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Very well. Your Honours should know that Shukri Buja gave evidence in another case, in the Limaj case, and was called by the Defence and was effectively turned hostile at the application of the Prosecution in respect of part of the history he gave about 1998, but nothing, as I am advised, that related to what is said in the statement he gave in relation to these proceedings, but you should certainly know that and have it in mind, if it's judged helpful in any way to the accused. Your Honours, I have had provided copies of Shukri Buja's 1990 -- 2001 statement, although it's an existing exhibit, as it occurred to me it might be helpful for you to have it recopied as I hadn't asked you to bring it with you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going into the background to this limited extent, going back to 1998, Shukri Buja says that he was abroad at the time, a journalist, and he was in Switzerland, having been convicted and served some time in Kosovo for being a demonstrator, and he says this, Mr. Janicevic, he says that following the killings of the Jasharis in March of 19 -- of Adem Jashari in March of 1998, the KLA received quite an increase in support and a lot more people joined up. Just as a matter of fact, is he right about that?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he's right. I don't know how many people joined up after Adem Jashari got killed -- after the death of Adem Jashari, rather.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If we can lay on the overhead projector, please, page 4 of the statement, with copies for the Chamber, if they'd like them, and for the accused, of course. The B/C/S version of this does exist and it will be coming down to assist the witness if he wishes it, but at the moment I just want to see, if we look at his statement ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't believe you necessarily read English, and if not, I'm sorry we haven't got the B/C/S version for you yet, but he in his statement identifies seven zones of the KLA under Azem Syla, and as to number 6, identifies Nerodimlje, which included Lipjan and Stimlje. Does that appear to you to be about correct as an analysis of the structure of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the translation here. Azem Syla was the first commander of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Azem Syla from Kisna Reka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he -- this is the statement of Shukri Buja. He says that of the seven zones, the sixth was Nerodimlje and that included Stimlje and Ferizaj. Do you accept his analysis, in broad terms, given in this statement?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with that part of the statement. The zone of Nerodimlje included that area, the area of the SUP of Urosevac, but that zone was established only in the autumn of 1998, not, as you had put it, immediately after the killing of Adem Jashari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the top of the next page, please, Mr. Nort. The number of men attached --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Nice is asking the witness about Urosevac, and under number 6, Nerodimlje, there is no mention of Urosevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Ferizaj is the alternative name for Urosevac. You can see that on the atlas. Over to the top of the next page, please, Mr. Nort.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Buja estimated the number of men attached to zone 6 as between 1.400 and 1.700 at various times. Do you dispute that calculation by him, the commander, of the numbers available to him?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to our information, during the war, after the 24th of March, there were over 2.000 terrorists in the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you think he was better supported than he calculates. If we go over, please, Mr. Nort, to I think it's page 6 but it may be slightly different in this, the way the printout comes. He says -- yes, at the bottom of this page, dealing with the process of arming, that they -- between March and May of 1998, a big influx took place, and he explains that people had to be escorted to Albania to get weapons. There were about a thousand, mostly young people, escorted in groups of 2 to 300 per day. He said they had no difficulty in buying weapons but it was hazardous getting them back, with a lot of men being killed from ambushes. Does that fit with your recollection, being on the other side, of setting up ambushes to stop groups of KLA young supporters bringing their weapons in?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, you are talking as if you were the KLA spokesman. First of all, these young groups were not ambushed. They illegally crossed the state border. The state border is a line that is protected on both sides, guarded. On the other side, they had absolute support, on the Albanian side; and on the other side, of course they did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, let me make it quite clear: I'm not on one side or the other. As you know, this Tribunal prosecutes people on all sides of this conflict. I just want to know if what Mr. Buja said is true and accurate, that people came from Albania with weapons and the Serb forces tried to ambush them. Is that about right?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that they went to Albania, that they illegally crossed the state border, and that they came across military patrols or whatever the military did by way of organisation - I don't know whether they really had ambushes - but many managed to get in and vast quantities of weapons were brought into the territory of Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Pretty much what he says. Next page, please, Mr. Nort. Top of the page. He says that he was in command of two brigades, one on the Stimlje to Ferizaj area and one on the Kacanik-Strpce area. Does that fit with your recollection, by way of intelligence, of what Shukri Buja was doing?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from the month of November 1998, but excluding Strpce. In the area of Strpce they did not have a single brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, next paragraph -- move the page a little please, Mr. Nort. He says: "We had bunkers and trenches in the area above and around Racak. I was given the plans of the bunker and trench positions in the village, which I approved, and the work commenced in the beginning of December 1998." Does that fit with your recollection of what happened there?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our information indicated that it had started a bit earlier, a month earlier, that it was continued only in the month of November, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around Racak, around Belince, and down the Crnoljevo gorge by the road, on the left-hand side facing Prizren.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He says that the civilians and KLA soldiers dug the bunkers and trenches. Does that fit with your understanding, that it was civilians and soldiers who dug the trenches?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our information was that they were making the villagers dig trenches. They were coercing them, and they even kidnapped some for ten or 15 days so that they would complete the job, and then they would release them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. If we go on to the -- oh, he says in the next paragraph: "The bunker and trench positions were to protect the Luzak gorge and to offer an escape route for Racak villagers." Does that fit with your understanding of the purpose of the trenches?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you say the purpose of the trenches was if it was different from what Mr. Buja says?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose of the fortification of that area was to protect the terrorists from possible clashes with the police and the military and to protect the Luzak pass, the area of Luzak, because Luzak-Laniste was the main road, for their purposes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, clearly the trenches --

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could not protect the villagers, because practically there weren't any villagers in Racak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll come to that in a minute. And of course the trenches were there to protect the soldiers, and I accept that and I'm sure he does. If you go on, please, Mr. Nort, to the next page, top of the page, I think. Yes, well, actually in the middle of our screen he says that there was a company command in Rance and they had four houses there with about 30 to 40 soldiers. Is that about right?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our information was that there were between 100 and 120 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is he right about there being four houses that they had at their disposal?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how many houses, but our information was that they have a terrorist group there that involved between 100 and 120 members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He then, in the next paragraph, says that in July or August there was a Serb offensive and that they had to evacuate villagers from Zborce in the municipality of Stimlje and that that place was levelled to the ground as a result of shelling. Is he right that there was shelling at Zborce?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is right that they expelled citizens from Zborce. That's correct. And also, he's right that there was terrorist action in the area. However, that the village was razed to the ground, that it was levelled, he's not right on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Nort, if you could turn on, please, I think a couple of pages, and I'll see whether we -- could you go on two pages, please. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He deals, at the top of this page -- and I may be able to find it, I've now got the B/C/S, but I'm afraid that I may have difficult without Ms. Dicklich in finding the B/C/S parallel, so to save time I'll read it to you in English. He speaks of the officer killed in Dulje, in the Suva Reka municipality, and he says this: That he later learnt that the local Serbs put on police uniforms and took part in the attack on Racak as revenge. He got this information from civilians in Vitina. Now, just thinking back, and I'm going to pause then in my examination of this statement of Mr. Buja, is it the case that there were civilians dressed as soldiers or as policemen involved in the attack on Racak?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is an absolute untruth, not to say a pure lie.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Can we now, please, look at another --

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just one more thing, please. The way you translated it for me, he says that he learned about it in Vitina. Vitina is 35 kilometres away from Stimlje. It is a completely different municipality. The municipality and city of Urosevac are between the two and Vitina was the area of the SUP of Gnjilane at the time. How could he learn anything from civilians at that time?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Very well. Can we now look, please, at another source of information, this one contemporaneous. It's part of Exhibit 321. The Court may recall that the blue book as entered into exhibit is not entirely correctly or perfectly page ordered. It's always been a possibility that we replace it by a better ordered set but we haven't done that yet, so I'm using the exhibited document, and the page references for Mr. Nort can be found at the top right-hand corner. So we start with 13555.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What we have here, Mr. Janicevic, is a diagram prepared by the OSCE on a daily basis, with supporting statements, and they set out what's been happening on the day in question. And I just want to go through a few earlier entries before we get to Racak to see if you agree that they appear to be reporting things accurately. So although it's a little hard immediately to get used to the notation, if you look at the top, this relates to the 3rd of January, between midnight and midnight. And as to your area, you'll see a little box there with a number 2 there. That relates to Stimlje. And it says at 0900 hours their group 5 reported information about a murder that occurred in Stimlje and the deceased man, Enver Gashi, was shot by two assailants. Do you remember that incident?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I spoke about that incident here, as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Indeed you did. If we go on, please, Mr. Nort, and the pages run backwards in number, to 13553, and we'll lay that on the overhead projector. But before we do, as to the man Enver Gashi, do you remember a visit from the OSCE representative Tommy Olofsson on the 4th of January, the following day, when he spoke to you about this?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean before the killing of Enver Gashi?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my understanding, the previous day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, the following -- my mistake if it was, I apologise. Olofsson visited you on the 4th of January. That's the day after. Do you remember that visit?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Olofsson visited me practically every other day. I cannot remember the exact content of our conversation on that particular day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it right, putting this very briefly because it's only a peripheral issue, that they were of the opinion that in fact it was the Serbs who carried out this killing and they didn't necessarily accept the version that was advanced to the effect that it was the Kosovo Albanians who'd carried out the killing?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Olofsson didn't say that to me. He only asked me about this particular case, when it happened, who was killed, and whether we had any information about this. I said that we still did not have any information, that an on-site investigation had been carried out, and that we're searching for the killer, the perpetrator of that crime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that our assumption is that it's the terrorists.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we'll look just at one other page, 13553, and I'll read the relevant part of this to you. Again, it has the OSCE patrol giving an account of what had happened. I needn't go through it in detail, but saying that a witness overheard men in Serbian dressed in black civilian clothes, getting into their car, saying, "Hurry up," and driving off. Do you remember his raising that as an explanation for what had happened, that Serb speakers had been overheard?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean that Tommy Olofsson mentioned that explanation?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't remember him saying that to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Move on to another topic -- sorry?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. If I may.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second or third time we met to discuss this issue, specifically this case, we had already received information that this killing was perpetrated from a VW Golf vehicle that had been seized in the Dramjak village during the kidnapping of nine persons about a week before this event, and that corroborated our suspicion that it was the terrorists who were responsible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And indeed the OSCE monitors challenged the identity of the vehicle, challenged its colour, whether it was black or black and red. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said a moment ago I can't remember the colour. It could have been grey, maybe red. I don't know. It was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 13596, please, Mr. Nort. The last preliminary matter before we come to Racak.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But if you allow me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police did not know what kind of vehicle it was until they talked to his family - to his brother, I believe - and it was his brother who described the vehicle. There was no dilemma about the colour of the vehicle. We took the word of his brother, because he was the only eyewitness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 13596, last preliminary matter, please. Another report, this time for the 4th of January, your area, Stimlje, and it's said that, if we look at the box -- wrong page, I think. 13596 at the top. It may be 546. No, it's -- it's 546, Mr. Nort. My apologies. I misread it. 13546. This for the 4th of January, box number 1 in the top right-hand corner, says that an unconfirmed report was received on the 4th of January for Stimlje, that a truck with MUP passed through the town of Belince, firing weapons. No person or building was hit. But just try and give us a picture of events. Were things that bad by the 4th of January that your police would be driving through towns, just firing weapons?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, Belince is not a town, it's a village along the road from Suva Reka to Stimlje on the left-hand side. In that sector, terrorist attacks and provocations were a daily occurrence. They were carried out from trenches on the left-hand side of that road. I didn't hear of any such case as you describe. Maybe they fired as they drove through, but only if they were being shot at.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nort, page 13445, if my reading of the figures is correct, please. This is for the 10th of January, as you'll see, and if you look at number 2 in the bottom left-hand corner, it sets out that on this day RC1, a different group, reported a MUP patrol had been ambushed in the vicinity of Slivovo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Page 13426, please, Mr. Nort. For this day, the 10th of January, the OSCE reported that tensions remained high in the Stimlje area as a result of two ambushes against MUP patrols within three days. However, the KLA commander south of Stimlje said he had no knowledge of the second ambush, and so this might, in the assessment of the OSCE, suggest that the KLA command and control structure wasn't solidified. So two points: Were tensions indeed high as a result of ambushes at this stage on MUP patrols?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tensions in Stimlje itself were very high because the population was mixed. There were no tensions within the MUP, because there was no reason for that. It was not the first or the last attack on the police. I already said that on the 10th January, 1999, 25 members of the police, the army, and civilians were killed in terrorist attacks. Twenty-five were seriously injured. It's impossible -- it appears impossible to me that Mr. Shukri Buja didn't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So far we're finding accurate reporting from the OSCE, are we not? Nothing inaccurate in what they reported.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 13406, please, Mr. Nort. We're now on to the 11th of January, just a few days before Racak, and here we see, at the bottom left-hand corner, that team 5 reported that the VJ had positioned a combat team in the vicinity of EM, and the number is given, immediately to the west of Stimlje. Is it right that as early as the 11th of January the VJ were positioning themselves west of Stimlje?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army of Yugoslavia had positions west of Stimlje, according to the agreement. It didn't take up those positions then. It had held them there since the arrival of the verifiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if you look --

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since October.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that was on Canovica hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We may find more support for the accuracy of the OSCE reports at page 13396, then, on that topic, where the same position was slightly differently expressed, and they said this, as to the force to the west of the Stimlje, they said, "These are believed to be the same forces, VJ forces, that have been operating in the area since the KLA ambushed the MUP patrol on the 8th of January, killing three MUP. They have continued Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. to change positions daily but array themselves primarily south-west, towards suspected KLA positions in the hills to the south-west of Stimlje." Is that accurate to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true, and I'll explain why it's not true. The army had one combat group deployed on Canovica hill. The police had six observation posts in the gorge, that is west of Stimlje, along the road, and there were 30 people on each post. That is a total of about 200 men on those observation posts. The army did not move from that area. And I'm sorry I omitted to say this before: They had another combat group pursuant to the agreement in Dulje, and maybe verifiers noticed movement in that direction. And it's about ten kilometres from Dulje to Stimlje, not more. That unit also belonged to the 243rd Motorised Brigade, I mean the unit that was in Dulje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I may have time to deal with the question of whether the employment was strictly within the agreement later, but we'll move on to page 13387, please. Now, this -- sorry, 13387. If we look at this, please -- no, it's 13389. I misread the number again, Mr. Nort. I do apologise; my mistake. What the OSCE reported here at number 6 for Stimlje is that the KLA told them - that's the OSCE - that over a thousand people had been displaced in the vicinity of Stimlje, and the combat team, that's the OSCE -- I'm not sure about that -- first reported several days ago remains in the area oriented west south-west. Forget that. A thousand people displaced already by this time. Were you aware of civilians moving, being displaced by the 12th of January?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Can we now look at -- can we go back, Mr. Nort -- just leave the file where it is. Can we put Shukri Buja's statement back on the overhead projector at about page 11.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I have that statement in Serbian, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I'll try and find it for you and the right page straight away, if I can. Yes. It's at the foot of page 11. Coming your way. Okay. Foot of page 11. And if you could hand -- Mr. Nort, if you could take this for the witness, please. You see, what Shukri Buja says in his statement is that on the following day, on the 13th of January, and you can see it there in the B/C/S, he spoke to the villagers in Racak and told them of the dangers of a possible attack. He advised them to leave for their own safety, but many stayed as they believed they could flee when the danger arrived. Now, pausing there, do you accept that -- perhaps did you have knowledge of the fact that many villagers did indeed leave Racak on or about the 12th, 13th of January?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not accept that, and I have no reason to believe that civilians had to run away from the police. I really don't. Anyone who addressed the police for assistance received it. Shukri Buja is right when he says that they advised them. They advised them everywhere, including Malopoljce. They emptied the village there and set up their base. Racak is not the only case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It appears he is accurate in saying that he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The answer to the question is yes, by the sounds of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But just looking at this same part of his statement to try and get context, he says that Seselj was in the area - well, we've heard about that from him - and that he made an inflammatory speech. Do you remember Seselj talking about retaliation? Just from the previous paragraph, but do you remember Seselj talking about retaliation for the killings of Serb police officers?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please. Seselj has never been in Stimlje, and he doesn't even know where it is, let alone having made a speech there. I don't think that he even passed through, because he mostly travelled --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- to Pec or Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know about --

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean to say that he made a speech to the citizens of Stimlje from a helicopter, asking for retaliation?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, that's not what I'm suggesting and I suspect you know that. The speech, as is revealed in the statement, was in Pristina. Do you remember him making a speech in Pristina, seeking retaliation?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's go back --

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't hear about that speech he made in Pristina, as you say, and I don't know that he demanded retaliation. Seselj was here recently; you could have asked him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if we stay with the statement that you're looking at, and perhaps, Mr. Nort, you'll turn it over to the next page. He says that most of the villagers of Cesta had left the area, didn't know Racak was going to be attacked. "We had information from the people that had been arrested that an attack was going to happen but not where or when. The people who were arrested were only asked questions about KLA positions, weapons ... strength and power that we had." Pausing there, is it right that a lot of people were arrested and asked questions about KLA positions?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not true that many people were arrested --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, if you would allow me to finish. Even that is not true. They were certainly not brought in to be questioned about such things like the positions of the KLA, the composition of their units, et cetera. We didn't need that sort of information. We had operative sources in the very headquarters of Shukri Buja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's certainly true that a very large number of statements of one kind or another were produced by, for example, your subordinate Jasovic, weren't they, Jasovic and Sparavalo?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I ask you, what was the point of all these statements and reports that Jasovic and Sparavalo made if it wasn't to get information about the KLA? And indeed, in your evidence earlier, you said that people were arrested or detained and questioned, I think.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, they were arrested, they were brought in, and they were questioned. I'm not arguing with that. But it's not correct that the only reason, the only purpose for such questioning was to find out about the KLA. There were other things to interview them about, such as weapons, possession of weapons, mutual conflicts, thefts, other criminal offences. And by the way, they were asked about that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, there's not a great deal in the statements, as far as I can recollect, about these other matters, but the point that was put to you just now by Mr. Nice was they were asked questions about KLA positions, weapons he specifically mentioned, strength and power.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly they were asked about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So your blanket denial that a lot of people were not arrested doesn't seem to tie in with the evidence you gave us earlier.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, taking somebody in for an interview and arresting them are two different things. If you bring somebody in, or even invite them for an interview, that does not mean it's an arrest. An arrest, according to our law, implies detention, remand in custody for over 12 hours. That's what we qualify as detention. Taking somebody in was not regarded as an arrest, according to the laws that applied at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What was the law?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Taking somebody in for questioning is an operative tactical method in operational work. According to the Law on Internal Affairs and the Law on Criminal Procedure, a police officer was entitled to bring in a person whom he suspected of having links with criminals or having perpetrated a criminal offence, for questioning, after which the person would be released, and the questioning would make place on the unofficial premises.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And how long could a person be detained on that basis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is not detention. The questioning would take as long as necessary but not more than 12 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What is it if it's not detention when you compel someone to go to the police station to answer questions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm trying to tell you how it is stipulated in our law. Under our law, that was not considered to be detention. Detention started once a decision was issued --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: With all due respect, Mr. Janicevic, that's playing with words. If you compel someone to go to a police station against his will, then what can you call it other than detention?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Bringing in a person for an interview. That's what it was called under our regulations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'll leave it to you, Mr. Nice, to see if you can -- if you wish to even try, to get any clearer explanation than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before we come back to, perhaps, His Honour's question, could you look at the next sentence in what Mr. Shukri Buja says in his statement. Dealing with the people who were brought in, he said this: "None of them were KLA, and they were all badly beaten." Now, let me remind you about a couple of questions I asked you yesterday about your experience with other police forces, about whether the standards in your police force slipped below what was really the proper standard, and let me just remind you you were obviously in a state of crisis with some of your territory held by the KLA, some held by the MUP, the VJ, and the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What date is this, Mr. Nice?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: This is -- well, Mr. Buja's speaking generally, but the particular date is the 13th of January, so it's on or before the 13th of January that he's speaking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So take your time, Mr. Janicevic, before tying yourself to a position that you might think you have to give. Were people in your police station beaten up to give information?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This suggestion of yours, Mr. Nice, is not correct. I, as chief of the Secretariat of the Interior, or my associates were never addressed with a complaint about maltreatment or beating.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And let's go further with electrocution. Were people subject to torture by electrocution to provide information?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a blatant untruth. I assert this because if it had happened, I would certainly have known and the person who had done it would certainly not have continued to work in my secretariat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What month in 1995 did you start your position at Urosevac police station?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 15th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And before that, where were you?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was president of the municipality of Strpce.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We may look at it later, but did you -- first of all --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Would Your Honour just give me one minute.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's right, isn't it, that as a matter of law the police are obliged to respond to any form of public complaint about their work? Is that right, as a matter of law? Article 54, I think, of the inspectorate for monitoring legality of work. You have to monitor media reports and take action in respect of them. Right? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Spotlight is a magazine, a publication of which you're aware?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of it. Never heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. It's a humanitarian organisation's publication. Is that the sort of material that wouldn't find its way through to the police if it was disseminated in Belgrade to the ministries?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it would probably find its way through, but I never received one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can see it later, if we have the time, but a magazine in January or February, of Spotlight, gave a detailed account of electrocution by way of torture at your police station. Did nobody at your police station respond to that? Because by the law, they were actually obliged to do.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These stories about electrocution, you could hear rumours going round, even before, from members of individual groups, however, we never established nor did we ever find any such apparatus or device for electrocution of persons on the premises of the secretariat. So I say once again that is just a lie. It's a blatant lie and nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a minute. Pausing there.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If somebody came, especially -- may I be allowed to complete what I'm saying? For somebody to reach their goal, their objective, and the objective was to create chaos in that area and distrust in the powers that be, they had to do things of the kind that you're telling us about now. They had to disseminate misinformation, for example. And I have hundreds of Albanian friends, for example, and none of them ever said that they had heard anything like that or seen anybody who had suffered from any electrocution devices or anything like that. I have hundreds of friends, and I'm still in contact with them to this day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did these rumours -- when you say rumours of electrocution torture, presumably you're saying rumours of electrocution torture at your police station. Where do these rumours come from; within the police station or outside?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in my police station, no, that's not what I meant. Not in my police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll come back to this, but just tell me this: We've seen that Shukri --

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, may I add something? You're talking about just one police station. The SUP of Urosevac had four police stations or, rather, five under it; the one in Urosevac, in Stimlje, in Strpce, in Kacanik, and the police station for the traffic police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at Mr. Buja's statement, here he is in 2001 giving an account of people telling him they'd been held, detained, or whatever it may be, and beaten in order to give information. Just help me, if you can, and don't, of course, if you can't: Can you think of any reason why, when the Serbs have gone, been expelled, Mr. Buja should make this up as part of his account, why he should falsely say that people were complaining of being beaten up to give information? Can you give us an explanation for that if you want to?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shukri Buja, at the end of February, I believe, pursuant to orders from the KLA was appointed commander of the Karadak zone, and during his time, that is to say while he was the commander of the Nerodimlje zone, there were a number of killings, both of Serbs, Albanians, and Roma as well. There were kidnappings that have still not been cleared up. In the Gnjilane area, where he was until the end of the war, there were hundreds of Serbs and Roma killed, hundreds of persons kidnapped or disappeared without a trace. So think about it. Why would Shukri Buja talk about that? I wouldn't be able to sleep peacefully if I were in his place. Just give it some thought. If he's not in a position to clarify certain circumstances now, the truth will out. The truth will always out. It emerges of its own.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I shan't pursue that question any further because I haven't been given an answer to it, but there it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we go back to the file, please, of OSCE documentation, just to try and stay broadly chronological, and it's page 13377, please, Mr. Nort. That brings us through to the same day, the 13th of January. And on this occasion, according to box number 6, the KLA commander in Stimlje area told a reporting group that VJ forces were within 200 metres of KLA positions. The last position was in the vicinity of Belince, west of Stimlje. Now, is that, do you think, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whose positions were in Belince? I'm not quite clear about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: VJ. The VJ forces are within 200 metres of --

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were they, then?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. The army was at Canovic Brdo, hill, which was at least 700 metres -- a minimum of 700 metres from Belince.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we go to page 13372, please. Let's just recognise where we were while it's coming to you. There's an approach to battle and war with armed units on both sides, really serious things, with people dying and being killed, but this is what was reported to a combat team on the 13th of January, last three lines: "The KLA commander reported that villagers trying to get to Stimlje or to Urosevac are regularly arrested and tortured with electricity in an attempt to get information about the KLA from them." So here is a report to the OSCE, before Racak even, of torture by electricity, presumably at your police station, because Stimlje and Urosevac are likely to come to your police station. It's true, isn't it? Your police station was a centre of unlawful violence used against people who were detained.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true. Let me just tell you something, since you're speaking about bringing people in and detaining them. At one point, Tommy Olofsson came to see me about 9.00 in the morning, I don't know what day it was, and he asked me, he said, "I was informed today that a person was kidnapped together with a tractor and taken to the police station in Stimlje." I took a telephone -- I picked up the telephone in his presence, called the chief of that police station, asked who had been detained, brought to the police station, and why. The person was brought in with a tractor full of timber, of wood that he had stolen in the socially owned, state owned forest, and they reported it as a kidnapping. So the information that the verifiers received they should check out first and then write reports of this kind. And I claim that there was no torture, no abuse, no beatings, no torture by electricity in my secretariat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we go, please, to 13364, Mr. Nort. One day before Racak, the 14th. See how things are developing. Now, what is said here in box number 5, in the bottom right-hand corner, is that it was reported that fighting and shelling occurred at Luznica and Javor and that the VJ would not allow the KVM patrols into the area. Now, is there really any reason why the OSCE should have got that wrong?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. You would have to ask somebody else that. Luznica, Javor, they're on the territory, as far as I know, of Prizren, not Urosevac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We looked at them yesterday. Mr. Nort, could we go to 13359 for a little more detail. This was their calculation. They said that they -- "RC1 reported that explosions had been heard in the vicinity of Javor and Luznica since 0830 in the morning. When they sent a patrol to investigate, they were turned back in the vicinity of Dulje." And then they made this observation: "This could be the precursor of a major battle throughout the Stimlje area. A report at 2055 hours stated that the tanks firing on the above village were from the Urosevac Brigade." Now, tell us, please, when was the plan to attack Racak made? 14th, 13th, 12th; when?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Which village? I'm not clear on which village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Racak. When was that plan made to attack Racak?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The plan to attack Racak, there was never any plan, but there was a plan for anti-terrorist operation in Racak, and a proposal of that plan was sent to the Staff on the 12th of January.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, can you see the place of village of Javor and Luznica and Dulje as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's get it on the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: My understanding is they are in Suva Reka.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. The Suva Reka municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour will remember that they were referred to yesterday in the report of this witness himself, at least Luznica was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Horseshoe was mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And horseshoe. And if you look at page 11 of the map Exhibit 83, you'll find them - I suspect you've found them already - in row P, boxes 20 and 21.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But how the operation in Javor and Luznica could be related to -- as a precursor to Stimlje operation, there I have difficulty following that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the Racak operation part of a wider operation, Mr. Janicevic?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Nice. The Racak operation, or the anti-terrorist operation in Racak has nothing to do with Luznica and Javor. Well, take a map and have a look. It's an area of 50 kilometres, if not more. Now, you make out this horseshoe effect and let's see what it looks like on the basis of what you say. I explained yesterday that it was a printing error with the report we saw. It was Luzak, not Luznica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, help me with this before we move on, I'm trying to be chronological: It happens, doesn't it, that there was a meeting of very high officials in Pristina on the 15th of January. Do you remember that visit of the high officials meeting with -- the Serb government was meeting there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about that from the information media, but I don't know what happened at the meeting or anything else about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the decision about Racak was a decision of the Joint Command, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true. Not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, whose decision was it, then?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A decision of the MUP staff. What Joint Command are you referring to anyway?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Radosavljevic has been interviewed by the Office of the Prosecution, and he's also spoken on -- at length on the television in the "Death of Yugoslavia" film preparation -- preparation for the film "Death of Yugoslavia." And he's a policeman, isn't he, senior to you?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He's in charge?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the appointed commander of the operation on behalf of the Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By whom was he appointed, then?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The MUP staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well -- well, if only the MUP staff appointed him, tell us, please, how it was that the MUP and the VJ could act together in an integrated way without putting each other at risk. How did that come about?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said during the examination-in-chief that on the 14th of January a meeting was held in the -- on the premises of the SUP of Urosevac, attended by Radosavljevic and all the participants in the operation and Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the command -- the Commander Krsman Jelic was called of the 243rd Brigade, where the plan was put forward for an anti-terrorist operation, it was proposed and he took note of that by way of information so as not to intervene at any point in time when the police starts entering Racak and takes steps to effect a blockade. The role of the army in this case, in this particular anti-terrorist operation, was just that, nothing more. I have no reason to lie. I have no reason to cover up anything, not a single reason.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if it be the case, can you think of any reason why Radosavljevic should attribute the Racak operation to the direction of something called the Joint Command?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think he would have any reason to do that, because links with what you referred to as the Joint Command, although I don't know that anything like that existed, had no links at all, nothing to do with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's look, please, at some entries for Racak itself from OSCE to see how much they appear to have seen. Mr. Nort, if you'd take us, please, to page 13354. This tells us -- this is for the 15th of January, and this tell us that there was a report -- bottom right-hand corner -- it tells us two things, actually. If we look at number 6: "The VJ are constructing and camouflaging a new position in the vicinity near the Dulje pass." That's to the west and in the area of both Dulje and the other place we were looking at. But as to Racak, it says: "Reported at approximately 0700 hours, fighting and shelling started south-west of Stimlje in the villages of Belince, Racak, and Malopoljce." They seem to be about right there, don't they?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are absolutely not right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What, no attack on --

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And here's why, and here's why: From 0300 hours, the Operative Pursuit Group had already entered Racak, and 30 men, 30 policemen of the pursuit group were behind the lines held by the terrorists, and they were in Racak. Do you really think that somebody would be mad and start shelling the village, bombing the village in which his own men were located? And I also state with full responsibility, based on reports and from what I heard because I was at a distance of 200 metres from Racak, that not a single shell fell in Racak, not a single shell coming from the army or the police that day until the afternoon hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how -- 200 metres from Racak. What period of the day were you 200 metres from Racak?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at the police station there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Stimlje.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police station, that's where I was. 200 to 250 metres away from the entrance to Racak. That's the police station. That's where it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's the Racak police station or the Stimlje police station?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Stimlje police station is located at a distance of about 250 metres from the very entrance into Racak from the direction of the special institution there, 200 to 250 metres. If you don't believe me, take a look at the map and check it out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll see it later because I think we'll get some footage of the special hospital, probably, special institution. Well, let's look at something else that was revealed by OSCE. On page 13351, please, Mr. Nort. A bit more of the detail. This is how they were keeping an eye on the territory generally. Elsewhere they reported that a large convoy of 275 MUP was seen approaching Prizren, miles away -- kilometres away. The local chief of police stated this was only a mismanaged but otherwise normal monthly rotation of police officers, stating that they were being relieved to return to Serbia for a rest. However, the question was raised by OSCE, given the increased tempo of the battle being fought in the vicinity of Stimlje, this rotation should be closely monitored by KVM to ensure the additional police not being used as reinforcements. Now, it's right, isn't it, that by manipulating rotation of forces that was permitted by the agreement, you could temporarily increase the number of forces that were available. Was there on the 15th of January of 1999 an effort being made to increase the number of forces available because of the scale of this attack?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Nice. On the 15th of January there was a regular rotation of the observation posts where it was usually the policemen of the reserve force who were deployed there at those posts. So there was a shift rotation; those who were at the observation posts went home, and the new arrivals took up their duties, which lasted a fortnight. That was the regular fortnightly shift.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Following page, 13350, please, Mr. Nort. This is what OSCE themselves reported, and you've made the point that they were present and that their vehicles could be seen at some parts of the day. They say this: "RC5 reported that an attack by combined VJ/MUP forces started in the vicinity of Stimlje at approximately 0700 hours. The towns of Belince, Racak, Petrovo and Malopoljce came under attack. Fighting and shelling were heavy throughout the day. This attack follows the VJ/MUP build-up in the area which occurred last week after the KLA ambushed a MUP patrol. It follows on the heels of the VJ/MUP engagement of KLA forces for several days in the Decane area. It is expected that this battle will continue tomorrow. KVM patrols are, for the most part, being denied access to the battle area." Now, that's a quite specific series of observations by OSCE about shelling throughout the day and where. Are you saying this is completely false?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only thing that is correct here is that Racak was dealt with in an anti-terrorist sense. Everything else is not correct. I don't know what the purpose of this is, but it is pure untruth, and I claim again and state that not a single soldier was engaged in this anti-terrorist operation. The verifiers were informed. They were at the posts as of 7.00 a.m. Later on, at 10.00, another Verification Mission vehicle arrived and they were there throughout the day while this operation lasted at the observation post. And that particular vehicle, after the attack launched by the terrorists against the police who were in Racak, it drove down into Racak. If they are objective, if they are even a little objective, they should have told the truth. And the truth is this: The truth is that it was only the forces of the MUP who entered the area of Racak, that it was a pure police operation, that the terrorists -- they started to arrest the terrorists, however, a clash broke out, a conflict, and what happened happened. There was no shelling, and I state again - I state again - that not a single shell fell on Racak. Had it fallen, some of the policemen would probably have been killed, some of the men who were there --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, the OSCE would have received this by way of a report. It says RC5 reported so-and-so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Who is RC5?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It's Regional Centre 5. It's their team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's their team.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes. If Your Honour looks -- remembers the maps with the squares, the various observation teams are described by RC1, RC2, RC3, RC4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: They are getting reports from their own teams.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Their own people, yes. Of course, they sometimes report what they have been informed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I'm not inviting you to attribute --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat his answer, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please repeat what you just said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The information was received mostly from the citizens, from citizens of Albanian ethnicity living in that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So for that reason you're saying it would be coloured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not only for that reason but I do claim and state that, objectively speaking, it was only in Racak that things happened that happened, but not as it is written down there. There was no shelling. Yes, the police did enter. Yes, they did search the terrain. Yes, they did fight with the terrorists. Yes, a certain number of terrorists did die in the clash with the police, but there was no shelling until 11.00. At 11.00 there was a cannonade from mortars coming from the Luzak area, Petrovo and that Crni Put as they call it, from the direction of Petrovo and Malopoljce. The first shell that fell was a mine from a 60-millimetre mortar, theirs, their mine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, you said that there were a couple of VJ positions around Racak, one in -- one to the north of Racak, which is the position of 243rd Motorised Brigade, and one to the east of Racak. I don't remember the name of the hill, but they were positioned there. Could you give me the total strength --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- of VJ which were positioned around Racak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Around Racak?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were two combat groups, one at the very entrance in Belince, which is 3 to 400 metres away from the entrance to Racak. Next to the police checkpoint that was there, there was also a military checkpoint, and it served to protect the communication lines, the roads, because that's where there were frequent attacks launched by terrorists; on roads, on military convoys, patrols, police patrols, and citizens. So that was -- they had a Praga there. How many men man a Praga, I don't know. Probably four or five. And there was another checkpoint at the hill called Kostanje which is about two and a half to three kilometres away from Racak. So that's where they were. They were above the church and school building in Stimlje. And that's where the observers were of the Verification Mission, next to them on that location, and next to the others too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: They had Pragas; did they have a tank as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether they had a tank. All I know is that they had two Pragas at both checkpoints. There was Praga at each point. But those points were not established that day, set up that day. They were checkpoints that had been there for a month prior to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you do not say that they didn't have a tank. You don't know whether they had a tank or not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether they did or not. I was informed that it was a question of Pragas being there on both those points.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I thought you were only 200 metres from Racak, from where you would be able to see where they were. So either they did or they didn't have tanks. Which is it? Or wasn't there a window in the police station that gave you a view?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, this way we will never be able to reach the end. Could you please put a map up so that I can show you where Racak was, where the access roads were, et cetera. When I arrived at the police station in Stimlje on the hill of Kostanje, I saw a police patrol and a military patrol, a military checkpoint which was there, which had been there a month before that, and it was supposed to protect that part of Stimlje from possible attacks by the terrorists. The other checkpoint was at the pass near Belince, facing Racak. That's where the Praga was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We will adjourn now for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: --- Upon resuming at 10:57 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I want to move on to -- I'm staying chronological wherever I can, but I want to play, to remind us, extracts from a Defence video which is said to be the Reuters Defence video for the 15th of January. That's the way it's been indexed, I think. And at the time that it was produced we hadn't made any inquiries. I'll explain what our current position is when we've had a look at it and I've asked a few questions, but I'd ask Mr. Reid to play selections of this, or organise the playing of selections of this on Sanction just to remind you of what it contained in general terms, and we'll stop at the place where the OSCE vehicles are said to be seen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps you'd look at this, please, Mr. Janicevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just pausing there. That thing is said to be, although it doesn't show up very well, the OSCE vehicles, and we can see vertical structures beside them and a building to the left. I'll go back to the beginning and we'll just look at various clips from this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: That's an overview in daylight hours of the village. Here we see a vehicle going through the village, again daylight, armed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this is a video that's been played to us in the course of the Defence as coming from Reuters and as relating to the 15th of January. Do you know one way or another if that was taken on the 15th of January or on a subsequent day?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was on the 15th of January, because on the following day we did not have any access to the village. The next day, the village never entered -- the police never entered the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Janicevic, just as a matter of detail to help you and to remind the Court, the way this has been provided to us is without soundtrack, so we don't know what the broadcasters were saying. There's plenty of material, I accept, not only coming from you but also from Radosavljevic in his interview and possibly even elsewhere, to suggest that Reuters and AP and other journalists may have been around on the 15th, but at present Reuters are unable to accept, I understand, that they had any footage on the 15th. So we're left in a state of uncertainty as to where this material comes from. With that information, and I think I'm giving you all the information that's available to me, when we saw the soldiers moving through the village, of course they were armed but there was either little or no sound of fighting or anything of that sort, and it looked not exactly peaceful but it looked comparatively safe, from what we could see. Can you explain at what time of day this was or anything else about what it is we've been asked to look at by the Defence, because it's a Defence video. Can you tell us what it really shows?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what else to say to you. We can see that it's daylight, most probably in the morning hours. The verifiers' vehicles can be seen here. I'm not mistaken, two or three of them at the same spot, as far as I can see on the picture that we can see now, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is, of course, no guarantee that the vehicles, even if this is the 15th, there is no way of asserting or knowing at what time the OSCE vehicles got into position. And if I were to suggest to you that OSCE monitors Marcusson, Giovanni, Fantini and Rose Jendensten, and maybe others, didn't locate until about 10.45 in the morning, would you accept that?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps some of them didn't arrive, but I claim that two vehicles of the verifiers were up there by the checkpoint, this police checkpoint here, at 7.00 in the morning, and also on the road to Kostanje. Two vehicles belonging to the verifying mission were there at 7.00 in the morning. Later on, I was informed that at about 10.00 another vehicle came and positioned itself there. It's probably that person called Giovanni as you said just now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you see the -- do you know what is meant by "hill 685," by the way? It may be an OSCE reference rather than a reference you may understand. Do you understand what they would be referring to by "hill 685"?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably an elevation, but I don't know which one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you see, I'm going to suggest to you that, as we saw in their report for the 24 hours of the 15th of January, throughout the afternoon they saw tanks and mortars firing towards Petrovo, Malopoljce. Do you accept that that was happening?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I do not accept that because that's not the way it was. There was shooting, there was mortar fire, but from the other side. I skimmed through this statement now. Shukri Buja himself says that mortar fire started around 11.00 from the direction of Petrovo, firing at Racak. There was mortar fire indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's look at Shukri Buja's statement next, still staying with the 15th of January. And it's about page 12, I think, in the English, my version still being slightly different from the one on the screen, but never mind. And the way, in summary, Shukri Buja analyses the day is that he says: "On the morning of the 15th --" next page, please. No, bottom of the page, thank you. On the morning of the 15th, the shooting began about 6.00 to 7.00. They were in a bunker. They had soldiers there. He said that the Serbs got to their positions -- next paragraph. Yes, it's there. That they -- three rounds were fired from his gun to signal there was a problem -- from their gun, the KLA gun, to signal that there was problem. Enver got killed pretty well immediately. This is at the bottom of the page. There were 47 soldiers there since October to November 1998. If we go over the page, please, Mr. Nort. Then he explains that -- third paragraph: The soldiers left the house and headed for their positions, were sure that their army would be there. They were in a crossfire. They tried to escape. Those that survived managed to get over the hill to Luzac. Then the unit commander, Afet Bilalli, nicknamed Qopa, as you've told us, was shot and injured. Now, all of that, no reason to doubt his accuracy there, is there?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shukri Buja is partly telling the truth, that --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which part of it is untrue?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I understood this correctly, because I didn't understand the translation sufficiently. Could you please give me a reference in the Serbian text so I can follow it. You read out an entire page and now I'm supposed to remember all of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's see if we can find it for you just a little bit more slowly. If you go to your page 12, and if you look at the -- first of all, if you look at the second paragraph on that page, you will see the description of their having 47 soldiers there since November 1998. In the paragraph above that you'll see the reference to the bunker and to the heavy machine-gun in the bunker. If you go to the foot of the page, you'll see a description of the soldiers leaving the house and getting caught in crossfire. And if you go over the page, you'll see, I think, maybe at the foot of that page, you'll see a reference to Qopa being injured. Is there any part of this that is actually untrue or is this conceivably completely accurate, subject always to such difficulties as there are --

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apart from the number of soldiers. Apart from that, I think that what else Shukri Buja said was correct. The number of soldiers, according to our verified information, was 80 in the area of Racak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we to over to what is I think still page 13 on the English and 13 in your version, please, we see -- further down or the next page, Mr. Nort, I think, maybe. Mr. Nort, next page, please. I think. Top of the page. Sorry, it is the foot of the previous page. My mistake. Last paragraph on the previous page. And for you, Mr. Janicevic, page 13. You'll see at the top of the page a reference to Sadik Mujota, where he says this: "Another two soldiers, Sadik Mujota, from Mullopolc, was staying with his relative and also a soldier Mehmet Mustafa, 62 ... in Racak, this house is located above Sala Mustafa's house and the command is located below it in the direction of the village. They were leaving the house for the direction of the shooting when they were shot. They were attached to the Racak unit. When the firing started it was the duty of all soldiers to go to the command and that is what they were doing at the time." And then this: "After Sadik was killed, his 15-year-old daughter, Hanumshahe, was killed while running to him. She fell on top of him. She is the only civilian that is buried with the soldiers." Now, no reason to doubt him on that, is there?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is reason to doubt that this was a civilian. Secondly, have you thought about where Sadik Mujota came from? He's from the village of Malopoljce. Malopoljce is two and a half kilometres away from Racak. What was he doing in Racak? He and his son and his daughter, we had information that from the very beginning, from mid-1998, were in the terrorist organisation of the KLA. All three of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, there's no challenge that -- sorry, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It says that plainly. Where is the problem?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Janicevic, there is no doubt that Sadik Mujota, who the Serbs regarded as a very serious terrorist, we know that, was a member of the KLA. What's in dispute, maybe, is whether his 15-year-old daughter Hanumshahe was a civilian or a member of the KLA. Now, he says she was innocent. She was running towards him. He was staying in the village. Isn't he right about that?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, I'm saying yet again we had information to the effect that Sadik Mujota, his son, and his daughter all belonged to the KLA. That they were in Racak, that they were in Racak where they belonged to the substaff of the Racak group of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, indeed there are documents going to suggest that his daughter is - or was - involved in the KLA, and we'll be taking you to those in due course, but what do you say was the level of your intelligence about her being a member of the KLA? Remind us or remind yourself and tell us.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of what I know, I assert that she was a member of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Detail -- Mr. Janicevic --

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I assert that she was a bit older than 15, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On any reckoning, this was a young woman or a teenager who is dead. So would you --

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, with a rifle in her hands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please do us or her memory the courtesy of giving us the detail of why you say she was a member of the KLA when the KLA commander says she wasn't. The detail, if you please.
