Until the investigation was completed, I as an authorised official did not have the right to give any further information except for what was said to the public by the investigating judge. Had the investigation been completed, the investigating judge would have given the exact number of terrorist casualties and everything that happened on the ground, but I cannot give a different explanation. The fact that the dispatch went on the 15th, on the evening of the 15th, I said that this was a dispatch that was still not accurate. This was information that was gathered from the field and that was being checked out. This is information that arrived after the anti-terrorist operation in Racak was completed, and that is checked only through an investigation and at the end of the investigation. This dispatch is of an internal nature in order to inform the MUP staff only, and the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the absence of any document supporting the suggestion that only 15 were identified at any time between the 15th and 16th, whether coming from this witness, coming Danica Marinkovic, or anyone else --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, that's not what I said. I did not say that they had been identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I was addressing the Court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: In the absence of any document supporting the suggestion, I can probably take this line of questioning no further in light of answers I'm getting. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But what I would be grateful for you now to look at, please, Mr. Janicevic, is the same document you're looking at, and a couple of paragraphs before the paragraph that deals with 50 and 15, where you say this: "They were also told --" Up, please, Mr. Nort. "They were also told that the police had not chased the terrorists beyond the trenches and connecting trenches, towards the woods, except for a group of policemen who had been sent to neutralise the Browning and who had carried out the assignment and returned to the centre of the village. As they were returning to the village, they had been under fierce fire and so the investigation team could not continue the on-site investigation ..." So that from your note of what you told -- no, let's go back to the previous paragraph as well. It's the end of the previous paragraph, please, Mr. Nort, a bit further up. The other way. Up. Down, then. You're quite right. Perfect. The -- you relay what you told the OSCE in these terms: You describe the, as you say, attack, and you deal with the distance of 500 metres from the trenches a heavy machine-gun. "Having searched the village, despite fierce resistance from the terrorists who had dug in, the police took control of their positions and liquidated a number of terrorists, while some terrorists withdrew in the direction of Krsine hill." So if you put that passage and the following paragraph together, there is no evidence of people being killed in the streets or in houses, and it appears that everyone who has died, apart from any who were killed at the machine-gun point, has died in a trench. Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do not accept that, but I do accept that they got killed near the trenches, most probably; either in the trenches or near the trenches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And indeed it's from the trench or from the base that all the weapons were seized.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the reports I received, right next to the terrorists who were killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the trenches. And if we go back to tab --

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And next to the trenches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's now go back, if we can, to what was tab 9, just to see how the OSCE recorded the same thing. You see, the OSCE recorded this in a broadly similar way. Said: "15 terrorists killed. Tried to find them, no one in village, went to forest and bunkers little bit up from village. Believe their central HQ in Juznice where a large group opened fire with a 12.7 millimetre gun. KLA used snipers, Chinese MGs, fired mines towards police and Chinese 81-millimetre mortar." Then this: "Over the hill ..." Then this: "Police searched until ... bunkers, stopped because of fire, and after forcing personnel out of bunkers who ran over hill, finding weapons ..." All right. Same again. Killed in the bunkers, weapons in the bunker. Do you accept that's what you told the OSCE?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you now look, please, at this document, which is -- in the collection of papers known as the Racak papers it's tab 33, but it's Exhibit D299 tab 397, introduced through Stevanovic, and I think not otherwise available to us until then. This is a document that you spoke of, and perhaps you'd just remind us what it is. That's the -- can he have the B/C/S original, please. It's a chronology of events in the village of Racak. I want you to look at it and confirm that you know what it is.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It is very difficult for the interpreters to follow with all the shuffling.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Very sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The Judges were asked to ensure that their mikes are off when they are not speaking, and the other parties should do the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just remind us, please, what this document is. It doesn't have a date on it. It was produced by the witness Stevanovic, Obrad. Would you tell us what it is, please.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the chronology of events in the village of Racak, a document that I drew up after the event upon the request of the district public attorney and the Ministry of the Interior. The last page bearing the signature is missing. 19th January.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So by the 19th of January, then, you had a pretty good idea, from reports coming to you, of what had happened, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those reports were reflected in this document, chronology.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And I only want you to look at one place. I'll just find it for you. In the English version it's on page 3, and for you, Mr. Janicevic, it is on the second page and it's the third paragraph and the fourth paragraph, I think. Fourth and fifth paragraphs. It goes like this: "Despite the --" oh, by the way, perhaps we ought to focus on the previous paragraph since you've drafted this yourself. Did you draft this carefully? Did you?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as carefully as I was able to do at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you see Luznica turns up again in the previous paragraph, the place you say is of complete irrelevance. Here you have got police force members approaching the village of Racak and attempting to capture members of the terrorist gang and inviting them to surrender. And they retreated from the village towards Krsine hill, the village of Luznica. The operation was perhaps rather larger than you've described in your recently produced maps, wasn't it? It covered a much wider territory, and it's impossible for to you acknowledge the truth of that.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just tell me on which page I can find that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. It's on the second page, and you'll find -- I think you'll find Luznica mentioned at the end of the fourth paragraph, probably. Yes. One, two, three -- the end of the fourth paragraph, where you see Luznica, Rance, Petrovo, and Stimlje all referred to.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that, but it's a typo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, it's another typo?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It cannot be Luznica by any means. Please, Krsine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... typographical error?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person who typed this, the typist who did this does not distinguish between Luzak and Luznica. Look at it and compare for yourself: Luznica, Krsine, Rance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Luzak is -- Luznica is 15 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The other places are close by. We're just mentioning villages around Racak. Rance is a village. Petrovo is a village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Despite the pursuit and the appeals to surrender, the terrorist group refused to surrender and kept opening heavy fire at the police force members from all the stated types of weapons. The terrorists fiercely attacked the approaching police from the previously prepared trenches and bunkers. Forty Siptar terrorists, most of them wearing uniforms of the so-called KLA, were liquidated in the said exchange of fire." First point: It was 60, it's gone down to 15. It's now gone up to 40, which is pretty well spot on for the number of people who died who were not acknowledged as KLA, couple under. How did we get 40 Siptar terrorists?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the number established after the completion of the on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's read -- would you be good enough to read for us, please, the first sentence - it's a quite long sentence, so fairly slowly - of the next paragraph.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "By capturing the trenches and bunkers used by the Siptar terrorists, apart from the said bodies, the police force members also found and seized 36 automatic rifles of Chinese make, one Browning 12.7-millimetre light machine-gun, two machine-guns, 1.802 bullets of different calibres, six hand grenades of Chinese make, two hand grenade bags, one Fisher Price hand-held radio transmitter, one pair of binoculars, one rifle-cleaning kit, two automatic-rifle magazines, one army rucksack and other military equipment. Apart from the bodies, a large number of cartridge cases of different calibres, which the terrorists fired at the police, were also observed and seized. The battle with the terrorists lasted until 1530 hours."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is no doubt, is there, from reading, as you would say, a carefully prepared report on the information available that all the people died in the trenches and all the weapons were found in or around the trenches. That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which brings us back, then, to the plans that we started looking at yesterday made by you and your colleague in his flat. Would you like, please, to point us to any document, and we can go through all the documents in the Racak collection, we can go through all of your documents, but you must know, can you point us to any document generated at any time until the maps you and your colleague prepared in his flat about three and a half weeks ago, that suggests people were killed in the ravine, on footpaths, in houses, on streets, or in yards?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you that because I don't have any such document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you yesterday, or maybe another day earlier on, that this was drawn up based on what is remembered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just focus on my question, if you can be -- if you wouldn't mind. If what you and your colleague are saying is accurate, then these documents that you produced are inexplicable because your colleague, through you, shows that people died all over Racak, not just in trenches, and I want you to tell us whether we can find any document available to you, written by you that suggests people were found other than in the trenches.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the document that I wrote based on the reports who were there on the ground. That's one. Second, have you ever been to Racak, Mr. Nice?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're not allowed to ask me questions -- well, you're allowed to ask me questions, but I don't answer them, but Mr. --

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I want to tell you --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- Janicevic, you can assume that I have some knowledge of the area.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I want you tell you that there were two rows of trenches in Racak, in the village itself. There was one bunker in the village, within the village of Racak itself. Look at the photos made by your own people --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- how the trenches are laid out and where they lead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I first saw that yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I think you've confirmed that so far as you are concerned, all the people died in bunkers -- in trenches. Now, perhaps the usher would be good enough to take one of the --

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or the immediate vicinity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or the immediate vicinity, yes. Of course. If you would take the large map.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think Mr. Nice is asking his questions improperly. If you look at the transcript, during explanations provided by Mr. Janicevic concerning the maps, he used the word "bunker" or "shelter" at least ten times explaining the maps, not "trenches." He was saying bunker, bunker, bunker, shelter. That word was widely used in his explanations. Communicating trenches are something different. In the chronology document, in here, reference is not really made to communicating trenches. It's not about that. It's something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have a look at the map that's on your right-hand side now, or the aerial view. Have a look at it. Do you know what it is? Forget the blue stickers for the time being. Do you know what that map shows? The little figures, 2, 5, 1, 4. Do you know what that map, that aerial view is?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Racak village. I can't see the numbers. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Forget the little blue stickers for the time being, but look at the numbers: 6 on the hill there, 4 on the left, 5, 2. Do you know anything about what happened at those locations?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is part of the settlement, part of the populated area in Racak. That's where the populated area begins. That's where the village of Racak begins.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where does the village of Racak --

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The map is not very clear, to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Well --

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The village of Racak is this part, and this too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your -- I've mislaid my maps. Can we look at the maps, Exhibit 70, that you produced yesterday. You don't recognise an aerial, but you appear to recognise -- that's all right, I've found them. These maps. Do you remember these maps?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can use that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can sit down. We'll hand them to you. Now, you say the aerial isn't very clear, but do you understand the map any better?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The image is clear but it's too large. I've never had occasion to work with aerial photographs before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if we look at your colleague's drawn map or overdrawn map and we remind ourselves that he, not you, has placed positions of deaths, people dying, all over the map; not just at trenches but elsewhere. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I have the map, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, it's coming your way. Exhibit 70. Well, I'm looking at 0300 to 0830. Then we'll look at the second one. The third one doesn't have any deaths -- oh, it does have some deaths on it, yes. Some of them are recorded as being at or near trenches, according to the legend, but others are nowhere near trenches. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this map, it's not right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we've tried to do our best to represent what's shown on your map by reference to where the bodies were found. Perhaps you'd like to look at this document. Yes, there are two or maps, but --

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even on the other map --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, what we find -- I want to distribute this as a visual aid. Obviously, like any visual aid constructed on the basis of a map as small scale as the one produced by the witness is, subject to possibility of error or inaccuracy. You see, your -- what we've done here, to explain it, is the following: The original map, at places like -- if you follow the original numbering on the map, 1, 2, 3, and then 3 is broken down into various sublocations, 3/6, 3/7, and 3/8; and 4, which is 4/9; 5, which is 5/10, 6 -- 5 is 5/10 and 5/11 and 5/12; and then 6, which is number 13, that original map shows the positions where bodies were found by OSCE on the 16th. Now, your colleague has drawn bodies being found, according to his memory, in certain locations. So that if we start off at the top, it's slightly obscured by the line, but the place 3/8, said by the OSCE to be a place where two bodies were found, Ijet Emini -- I beg your pardon, one body was found, we see that, according to your map, at roughly the same place some eight bodies were found. So 3/8, roughly eight bodies. If we go to the left of that, where the original map of the Prosecution was marked 4/9, which was a scene where, as the legend shows, one, two, three, four, people were killed -- sorry, three people were killed, he's recorded on his map, at roughly the same place, six bodies were found. If you go to the position marked 3/7, where the OSCE found two people, if we look at the top we can see that your colleague found, or says, that two people were killed there. Now, those are some of the most closer matches. There are several which are very distant in comparison. But one way or another, your colleague, for whatever reason, seems to have been placing bodies at roughly the places where the Prosecution said those bodies were found. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you look at the screen in front of you right now, you will see that Mr. Nice's question is taking up the entire screen. I don't know what this witness can possibly answer to a question that more resembles a lecture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice. It's time for you to put a question. We have had occasion to reprimand Mr. Milosevic for the same practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have explained the position of this map I hope in a way that will help.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what I'm suggesting to this witness is revealed by this map, is that for whatever reason your colleague was actually revealing that the bodies found by the OSCE on the 16th indeed probably -- or not probably, certainly died where they were found. Do you follow that?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand that at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... way?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I can see there are similarities between the one and the other map. There are similarities. I claim that the person who made this map did not have any opportunity to see the other, had no occasion or possibility nor knew of the other map's existence. He drew his map based on the reports and from his own memory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, until now the suggestion has been advanced, somewhat hesitantly from time to time, I think, that the Racak bodies were moved around after they died in order to make it look like a massacre. Well, what we know from your accounts given to and for the international community and certainly until the 19th of January on your own evidence was to the effect that everyone died in a trench or near a trench. The international community found the bodies spread all over Racak, none of them near trenches, and many or most -- many if not all of them photographed where they were found, and we'll look at those tomorrow. And your colleague, by this map, for whatever reason, is confirming that they were found scattered around the village and not in trenches.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never said that the international community said what you just mentioned. Please don't put words in my mouth. I never said that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My colleague, that's my second point, made his map from his own memory. I'm just responding to the question as it was interpreted to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Well, if it's ever suggested, Mr. Janicevic, if it's ever suggested that these bodies found in Racak were taken from their initial positions and moved around, that's not a suggestion you'd accept, is it?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't quite understand. Could you repeat it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Do you suggest that the bodies found by the OSCE on the 16th and photographed had been moved from their positions, or do you accept - you're the man in charge - that the OSCE found the bodies where they died?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not just that I don't accept that all of them were killed where they were found. A number of them were, but another number was moved. It is a fact that the bodies were manipulated --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and not by the police. Not by our side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... which ones were moved?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bodies that were found in the gully were moved. I had occasion to read Ambassador Walker's statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where from?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the Internet. I found his statement on the Web. I had an opportunity to see it, and I remember a portion where he says that he had been informed by a verifier that there is another number of bodies further up in the gully, and he was asked if he wanted to see them, and he said he had had quite enough. Why didn't he go there and record them then and there to clear it up, who did it and how it happened. If it was a crime, then perpetrated by whom? For one entire night, the bodies were left lying there in order to provide room for manipulation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, we have to end the hearing now. We will adjourn and resume tomorrow at 9.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
